name: St. Dorothy's Rest
meeting: Main hall 40' x 25' w/ stone fireplace; several smaller rooms + redwood chapel
buyout: Yes, whole site for groups of 68+
why: 1901 redwood camp: shingled buildings, fireplaces, sleeping porches, dining porches, chapel in the trees. Closest thing to a Lighthaven-style campus you can actually book.
watch: Mixed room types (single/double/dorm); dorm bedding costs extra
note: Research note: the retreats page lists per-building bed counts (Main House, Farmer, Lydia, Upper/Lower Miriam) and 2026 rates; 12-person minimum for meals; dorm bedding extra. Office hours Tue-Fri 10-5.

name: Green Mountain Retreat
meeting: Multiple meeting rooms; historically hosted groups of 5-200
buyout: Yes for a group your size
why: 66 acres in the redwoods with a redwood amphitheater, cottages, indoor and outdoor gathering areas. Under new ownership/branding since the Presentation Center era.
watch: Newer operator, so ask what has actually been renovated
subtitle: former Presentation Center

name: Westerbeke Ranch
meeting: Casa Nueva ~80 classroom style; several breakouts
buyout: Yes, explicit exclusive-use contract
why: Five-generation family homestead: adobe, Mexican tile, gardens, pool, hot tub, chapel. Warm and lived-in rather than corporate. Very close analog to SSS Ranch.
watch: Overnight cap is right at or slightly under 60, so a few people may need to commute or double up
note: Research note: meeting rooms on site are Casa Nueva and the Round House; cabins are color-named. The venue's photo library is low resolution, hence the softer images here.

name: Waterfall Lodge & Retreat
drive: ~1 hr 30 min (30 min from San Jose)
meeting: 150 day guests; big reclaimed-barnwood lodge
buyout: Yes, whole-property rental
why: 80 private acres of redwoods with an actual waterfall, a hand-built lodge from 19th-c. reclaimed timber, meadow, bring-your-own-vendor policy. Design-forward and quirky.
watch: Mostly a wedding venue, so push them on conference AV and breakout rooms

name: Lodge at Marconi
meeting: 8 event spaces: Tower Hill 250, Buck Hall 100, Cypress/Pine 45 each, amphitheatre 40
buyout: Ask; property is small enough that 60 nearly fills it
why: 62-acre state historic park on a hillside over Tomales Bay. Site of Marconi's 1913 wireless station, later Synanon. Mid-century Bay Region architecture, recently and expensively redone.
watch: Priciest of the Marin options; oyster-country food scene is a plus
note: Research note: as of Aug 21 the hotel booking engine returns no rooms for any night Oct 1-29 (while late October onward is wide open), which looks like a closure or full buyout; the reason is not published, so ask.

name: The Land
meeting: Lodge plus multiple gathering spaces; scales to 250 with tents
buyout: Yes; they say they specialize in groups of 20-60
why: 162 acres of redwoods and a 5-acre organic garden, farm-to-table meals, river swimming. Explicitly built around groups the exact size you are running.
watch: Long drive; carpool logistics matter
note: Research note: the site now also brands the property as 'The Eros Monastery' with practice-infused stays; it is 18+ only and alcohol- and cannabis-free. Verizon has no signal on site (AT&T and T-Mobile do).

name: Camp Navarro
meeting: Great Hall 4,600 sq ft, seats 400 for dinner; kitchen for 500+
buyout: Yes, full site
why: Historic 1930s Masonite company camp in 200 acres of redwoods. This is where real conferences and festivals go. Enormous character, real infrastructure.
watch: Way bigger than 60, so you pay for scale you will not use; they explicitly do not take booking calls
note: Research note: the physical address is 901 Masonite Industrial Rd, Navarro. Booking inquiries go to inquiry@campnavarroca.com; site tours are by approved request only.

name: Enchanted Hills
meeting: Dining hall, breakout rooms, outdoor amphitheater
buyout: Yes, off-season group rentals
why: 311 acres of redwoods, creeks, ponds, a small lake, pool and amphitheater. Run by LightHouse for the Blind, so rental money funds the camp. Mid-October is their rental season.
watch: Rebuilt post-2017 fire; confirm which buildings are back online
note: Research note: now branded 'Enchanted Hills Napa'. Post-fire rebuild includes the Forest Commons dining/meeting hall, Hillside Village casitas, and Lakeside and Forest cabins plus tents and yurts.

name: Mount Madonna Center
sleeps: Conference Center 33 rooms / 74 beds; plus yurts, cabins, glamping
meeting: Conference Center 250 theater style; Seminar House 40
buyout: Yes for the Conference Center building
why: Ridge-top campus with views to Monterey Bay, 380 acres, very well-run retreat operation, vegetarian kitchen. Unusually organized for this price band.
watch: Ashram-adjacent aesthetic; some cabins have no plumbing

name: The Bishop's Ranch
meeting: Conference hall up to 125; smallest room 12
buyout: Yes, Exclusive Use groups get booking priority
why: Vineyard-and-oak hillside ranch above the Russian River, mix of a rambling Ranch House, a lodge and five cottages. Quiet, handsome, unpretentious.
watch: Hosts nonprofit groups only, so the organizing entity matters

name: Costanoa
meeting: Indoor rooms with patios plus outdoor/tented options; 150 capacity
buyout: Ask about buyout; shoulder season helps
why: Coastal bluff camp an hour from SF, surrounded by four state parks. Glamping-plus-lodge mix means you can flex the budget per attendee.
watch: Weather in mid-October on that coast can be cold and foggy at night

name: Saratoga Springs Retreat Center
meeting: Heart Lodge 2,400 sq ft; 30-ft yurt for 40
buyout: Yes, exclusive use for groups of 25+
why: Weird in a good way: a 19th-century round house mineral pool, stone labyrinth, fire circle, hot soaking pool, springs. Cheap for exclusive use.
watch: Rustic; 2-10 night minimums; farther out
note: Research note: the official site is a frozen 2020 page with tiny photos, so the gallery here is thin. The center is still operating (it hosted a festival in Oct 2025); site text says exclusive use for groups of 25+, 2-10 night stays, 260 acres.

name: Westminster Woods
sleeps: Groups of 20-200; dorm cabins, 3 guest lodges, private rooms
meeting: Multiple meeting rooms with wifi, dining hall
buyout: Yes for a group of 60
why: 200 acres of coastal redwoods on Dutch Bill Creek, next door to Occidental. During the school year they only take Friday-Sunday bookings, which is exactly your dates.
watch: Church-camp bones; dorm-heavy lodging

name: Monte Toyon
meeting: Day use 150; Helgesson Hall (stage, wood floor, good acoustics)
buyout: Yes at your size
why: Redwood camp minutes from the beach, run by UCCR so pricing is transparent and group-friendly. Meeting spaces are free for overnight groups.
watch: Plain camp aesthetic; less 'wow' than Tier A

name: Vallombrosa Center
meeting: 11 meeting rooms
buyout: Effectively, at 60 people
why: Walled 8-acre garden estate in downtown Menlo Park. Zero travel friction for a Bay Area crowd, walkable to town and Caltrain, private rooms for everyone.
watch: Restricted to religious, educational or charitable groups; suburban rather than scenic

name: NatureBridge Golden Gate
sleeps: Dorm lodging on two campuses (Bluff at Point Bonita, Beach at Fort Cronkhite); up to 200 guests total
meeting: 4 meeting rooms: Coast 20-49, Raven 30-62, Cypress 30-97, Sunset 50-130
buyout: Ask; with two campuses, 60 can likely have the Bluff campus to itself
why: A 5.2-acre former army post inside the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, ocean beaches and Golden Gate views out the window. Cheapest good option and absurdly close to the city.
watch: Bunk dorms and shared baths; institutional interiors. The YMCA no longer runs it: NatureBridge took over in Nov 2023, so the sheet's YMCA phone is stale
subtitle: former YMCA Point Bonita
note: Research note: the YMCA of SF closed this site; NatureBridge now markets it as the Golden Gate Conference & Retreat Center. Published 2026 rates are about $157-162 per person per night ($136-141 for nonprofits). Overnight availability is Fri-Sun during the school year, which fits Oct 16-18.

name: Walker Creek Ranch
meeting: Conference center plus multiple meeting rooms
buyout: Yes, they take private conference bookings
why: 1,741 acres of West Marin ranchland run by Marin County, big open space, dark skies, low cost.
watch: Primarily an outdoor school; ask what else is on site that weekend
note: Research note: the conference-center contact on the site is (415) 491-6603 / jparker@marinschools.org (the sheet had the main office line). Lodging is four lodges with 2-5 bed rooms, 13 bunk cabins, two bunkhouses and camping.

name: Harbin Hot Springs
meeting: Event spaces for gatherings and workshops
buyout: Group retreats hosted regularly
why: Eight thermal pools, 1,700+ acres of land, EcoFarm, deeply countercultural. Memorable in a way a hotel never is.
watch: Clothing-optional culture; you would need to brief attendees; not a polished conference plant
note: Research note: the post-2015-fire rebuild is still in progress. A new restaurant opened in August 2026 and a new multi-story hotel is being finished; current lodging is domes, hotel rooms, caravans and tent camping. Harbin has not allowed group bookings since July 2023: every guest buys a membership and books individually, so a 60-person retreat here means 60 separate reservations.

name: Wilbur Hot Springs
sleeps: ~40-50 across historic hotel, cabins, bunk rooms
meeting: Common areas; no dedicated large conference hall
buyout: Yes, they do full-site buyouts
why: Off-grid solar lodge from 1915 on an 1,800-acre private nature preserve. Total disconnection, natural mineral flumes. Singular.
watch: Probably tops out below 60 beds; very limited connectivity

name: Asilomar Conference Grounds
meeting: Many meeting rooms; wood-beamed Crocker Dining Hall
buyout: No (state park concession), but you can block a wing
why: Julia Morgan's 1913 Arts-and-Crafts campus in the dunes on its own state beach. Architecturally the most Lighthaven-adjacent thing in Northern California.
watch: Shared with other groups; no TVs or phones in rooms; farthest south

name: 1440 Multiversity
meeting: 40,000+ sq ft, 30+ indoor and outdoor venues, up to 300
buyout: No, but all-inclusive group packages
why: Purpose-built modern learning campus in the redwoods: great AV, infinity hot tub, all-inclusive pricing with three meals a day. The zero-hassle option.
watch: Most expensive on this list; polished-wellness aesthetic rather than idiosyncratic
note: Research note: 1440 never sells a buyout; groups book room blocks under all-inclusive packages, and its Group FAQ says it has a waiting list for private mission-aligned group events.

name: Mendocino Woodlands
meeting: Kitchen/dining/rec hall per camp, campfire circles
buyout: Yes, you rent an entire self-contained camp
why: 720-acre National Historic Landmark, the only CCC-built 1930s group camp still operating as one. Looks exactly as it did in 1942.
watch: Very rustic and far; October nights are cold; you bring more of your own operation

name: Land of Medicine Buddha
sleeps: Max 56 (19 guest rooms plus yurts and camping)
meeting: Meeting halls, dining hall open 24/7
buyout: Yes, exclusive group rentals
why: 108 forested acres with a pilgrimage trail, quiet and cheap, 2-night minimum fits Fri-Sun perfectly.
watch: Caps at 56, so a few people commute or camp
note: Research note: the sheet's stay.landofmedicinebuddha.org booking link was returning errors; the working group-rentals page is on the main domain.

name: Presidio Lodging
meeting: Up to 200 attendees
buyout: Yes, full two-property buyout is an advertised product
why: A national park inside San Francisco: 19th-century brick barracks on the main post, Golden Gate views, everyone can fly in and Uber. The urban answer.
watch: Hotel rather than campus; no single big communal hall the way a camp has
subtitle: Inn + Lodge at the Presidio

name: Hidden Villa
meeting: Dana Center, Duveneck House, Morgan Pavilion up to 60; site holds 200 day guests
buyout: Day buyout yes; lodging is the constraint
why: 1,600-acre working farm and wilderness preserve in the hills above Silicon Valley, the oldest hostel on the Pacific Coast. Cheap day rates ($300-$850 per space).
watch: Only 39 beds, so this works as a day venue with off-site lodging
note: Research note: meeting spaces are the Dana Center, Duveneck House and Morgan Family Pavilion; the hostel sleeps 39.

name: Triple S Ranch
meeting: Multiple indoor and outdoor spaces, up to ~200 standing
buyout: Yes, exclusive use of the 14-acre estate
why: Your benchmark: restored antique barns, 1920s-50s cottages, a Victorian house, redwoods, pool, 20-person infinity hot tub.
watch: Listed for reference / price comparison
subtitle: your SSS example

name: Mayacamas Ranch
meeting: n/a
buyout: Not currently bookable
why: Was the iconic Bay Area exclusive-use retreat center until the 2017 Tubbs Fire. Now positioned as a 300-acre 'bioregional hub' seeking steward partners, not taking group bookings.
watch: Included so you do not waste time chasing it

name: Ratna Ling
meeting: n/a
buyout: n/a
why: Gorgeous Tibetan Buddhist retreat center in the coastal hills, but too small for 60. Noted so it does not come up again.
watch: Ruled out on capacity

name: Green Gulch Farm
meeting: 40 max
buyout: n/a
why: Zen Center farm in a coastal valley above Muir Beach. Gorgeous, but too small for 60, and not accepting new 2026 booking requests.
watch: Ruled out on capacity

name: Sea Ranch Lodge
meeting: n/a
buyout: n/a
why: Iconic 1960s modernist lodge on the Sonoma coast bluffs. Gorgeous, but too small for 60. Noted so it does not come up again.
watch: Ruled out on capacity

name: Menucha Retreat & Conference Center
subtitle: the 1927 Meier estate, Columbia Gorge
travel: Fly SFO→PDX (~2 h), then ~30 min east on I-84
sleeps: 126+ beds: Wright Hall 45, Ballard Hall 37, The Barn 32, Beam House 12, plus Creevey Complex and Boyd Hall; site capacity quoted as 1–140
meeting: Wright Hall Great Hall 90 on the main floor + 30 in the balcony; Ballard 40; The Barn 32; Greenhouse 32; several 8–20 person lounges
buyout: Likely — 140 capacity for a group of 60, and it runs ~200 groups a year; ask
why: Julius Meier's 1927 summer estate on a bluff over the Columbia Gorge: shingled estate house, rockery gardens, a pool on the bluff, and a barn and greenhouse that both double as meeting rooms. Non-profit conference-centre pricing rather than resort pricing, and 30 minutes from a major airport.
watch: Mixed lodging from private rooms to dorms; rates are not published anywhere, so everything starts with an inquiry form. Church-owned (First Presbyterian Portland) though it rents to secular groups.
note: Research note: physical address is 38711 E Historic Columbia River Hwy; mail goes to PO Box 8, Corbett OR 97019. Office hours Mon–Fri 8–4 PST.

name: Sleeping Lady Mountain Resort
subtitle: Harriet Bullitt's art-filled camp
travel: Fly SFO→SEA (~2 h) + ~2 h 20 drive, or SEA→EAT (Wenatchee) + ~45 min
sleeps: 58 guest rooms across clustered timber lodges — a 60-person group is essentially the whole resort
meeting: Nine meeting rooms, 10,000+ sq ft of function space, seating 30–190
buyout: Effectively yes at 58 rooms; inclusive group rates are the normal way it sells
why: A 1930s camp rebuilt by Harriet Bullitt into a campus of low timber buildings scattered through pines under the Icicle Canyon walls, with a serious Northwest art collection sited across the grounds. Inclusive per-person pricing means one number covers rooms, three meals and meeting space.
watch: The airport that is genuinely close (Pangborn/EAT) only flies to Seattle; the practical route is SFO→SEA and a 2 h 20 drive over Stevens Pass. Leavenworth is a Bavarian-theme tourist town in high season.
note: Research note: the site's photography is credited to Erik Sven Photography. The $195-per-person inclusive figure comes from a Cvent listing, not the resort's own page.

name: The Colorado Chautauqua
subtitle: 1898 cottages under the Flatirons
travel: Fly SFO/OAK/SJC→DEN (~2 h 20), then ~50 min to Boulder
sleeps: 59 cottages (studio to 3-bedroom) plus Missions House Lodge and Columbine Lodge; one lodge sleeps 16 in eight en-suite rooms
meeting: Community House, the lodges (one seats 35), the Dining Hall, and the 1898 Auditorium
buyout: No — the grounds are a public city park; this is a large room block plus meeting space
why: A National Historic Landmark and the only continuously operating Chautauqua west of the Mississippi: 26 acres of green-and-white Victorian cottages with screened porches, a dining hall and an 1898 auditorium, sitting directly under the Flatirons with trailheads at the door.
watch: Not exclusive-use, and the site's own copy pitches curated retreats for 10–50, so 60 needs a conversation. Cottages have kitchens but the lodging is spread across many small buildings. Boulder in October can be cold.
note: Research note: catering runs through the Chautauqua Dining Hall and Three Leaf Concepts. Founded 1898; one of only two National Historic Landmarks in Colorado offering lodging and events.

name: Rosario Resort
subtitle: Robert Moran's 1909 mansion, Orcas Island
travel: Fly SFO→SEA, then Kenmore Air to the resort's own seaplane dock or Orcas Island Airport (~10 min), or the Anacortes ferry
sleeps: Village rooms around the mansion — listings range from 69 to 107 rooms; no guest rooms in the mansion itself
meeting: Event space in and around the Moran Mansion on 30 waterfront acres
buyout: Ask — the room count is well above 60, so a full buyout is a real question rather than a given
why: Shipbuilder Robert Moran's 1909 mansion on Cascade Bay: copper roof, mahogany, stained glass and a working Aeolian pipe organ in the music room, with Moran State Park at the back door. The seaplane base is on the resort's own waterfront, which is about as close as an airport gets.
watch: Two-leg travel from the Bay Area (SEA plus a small plane or a ferry). The mansion is the beautiful part; the guest lodging is ordinary resort-village building stock, and the resort's own gallery could not be scraped, so the photos here are all Wikimedia Commons shots of the mansion.
note: Research note: coordinates come from the OpenStreetMap node 'Rosario Resort and Spa'; Nominatim could not resolve the street address. The resort changed hands recently and room counts differ between listings.

name: Hacienda del Sol Guest Ranch Resort
subtitle: 1929 adobe in the Catalina Foothills
travel: Fly SFO/OAK→TUS (~2 h), then ~25 min to the Catalina Foothills
sleeps: 97 rooms, casitas and suites, plus the 3,400 sq ft Casa Alcalde residence
meeting: 14,000+ sq ft indoor and outdoor: six meeting rooms, two convertible suites, four outdoor sites, and the 2,910 sq ft Casa Luna
buyout: Yes — the resort markets full buyouts
why: Opened 1929 as a girls' boarding school and then a guest ranch: purple-and-blue painted adobe arches, tiled stairs, stone walls and cactus gardens in the Catalina Foothills, with a library and a Historic Hotels of America listing. Twenty-five minutes from a direct Bay Area flight, and it will sell you the whole place.
watch: Luxury-resort pricing, and it is a working resort rather than a retreat centre. Mid-October is the start of Tucson's high season, so rates are near their peak.
note: Research note: room mix is 70 Sonoran, 10 Hacienda, 9 Historic rooms, 3 Historic suites, 2 Sonoran suites, 2 one-bedroom casitas and the Casita Grande.

name: Sundance Mountain Resort
subtitle: Redford's canyon village, Mount Timpanogos
travel: Fly SFO/OAK/SJC→SLC (~1 h 50), then ~1 h up Provo Canyon; Provo (PVU) is ~35 min
sleeps: Rooms, cottages and suites, and multi-bedroom mountain homes across the village
meeting: About 12,000 sq ft of indoor and outdoor meeting space, most of it glass-walled onto the canyon
buyout: Ask — mid-October is between leaf season and ski season, which is the best shot at holding the village
why: The place that invented the rustic-modern idiom everything else imitates: 5,000 acres in Provo Canyon under Mount Timpanogos, timber-and-river-stone buildings, cottages with stone fireplaces, and meeting rooms that open straight onto the mountain.
watch: The most expensive option here, and lodging is spread between the Inn, cottages and mountain homes rather than one campus. Redford sold his stake in 2020. A whole-village hold at 60 people is unconfirmed.
note: Research note: coordinates are Wikipedia's; Nominatim only resolved a ski run inside the resort.
